name: Economics
topics: Basic concepts: scarcity, choice, scale of preference and opportunity cost
Basic tools: tables, graphs and measures of central tendency
Theory of production and factors of production
Financial institutions, banking and the central bank
International trade and balance of payments
Agriculture and industry in West Africa

questions.q: In economics, scarcity simply means that:
o: All goods are given out freely without any payment
Human wants are unlimited but the resources to satisfy them are limited
People always have more money than they can spend
Government fixes the price of every good in the market
questions.e: Scarcity is the basic economic problem that resources (land, labour, capital) are limited while human wants are unlimited. This forces people to make choices. The other options describe situations that are not what economists mean by scarcity.
questions.p: Scarcity na say resources no plenty reach to satisfy all the wants wey people get, wey no get end. Na because of this one people dey choose wetin dem go buy. The other options no be wetin economist dey call scarcity.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why people must constantly make economic choices?
o: Because resources are limited while human wants are unlimited
Because goods in the market are always too expensive
Because traders always want to make more profit
Because the government controls every sector of the economy
questions.e: Choice arises because resources are scarce compared to the many wants people have, so people must select which wants to satisfy first. The other options are not the real economic reason for choice.
questions.p: People dey choose because resources no plenty well-well compared to all the many wants wey dem get. So dem go select wetin dem go first satisfy. The other options no be the real economic reason.

questions.q: A trader who has only ₦20,000 to stock either rice or beans must decide which one to buy for resale. If she buys rice, she cannot buy beans at the same time. Which basic economic concept does this situation best illustrate?
questions.e: Because the trader has limited money (a scarce resource) and two wants (rice or beans), she must choose one over the other. This decision-making under scarcity is exactly what economists call choice.
questions.p: Since the trader money no plenty reach buy both rice and beans, she must pick one. This kain decision wey person dey make because resources no reach everything na wetin economist dey call choice.

questions.q: Opportunity cost in economics refers to:
o: The tax government charges on imported goods
The total amount spent on producing a good
The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
The market price customers pay for a good
questions.e: Opportunity cost is not just any cost; it is specifically the benefit lost from the next best option that was not chosen. The other options describe price, tax or production cost, which are different concepts.
questions.p: Opportunity cost no be just any cost; na the value of the second best option wey person no choose. The other options dey talk about price, tax or production cost, wey no be the same thing.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State has only one plot of land for this planting season. He estimates that maize would earn him ₦60,000, yam would earn ₦50,000, and cassava would earn ₦45,000. He finally decides to plant maize. What is his opportunity cost?
o: The combined value of cassava and yam, ₦95,000
questions.e: Opportunity cost is only the single next best alternative sacrificed, not the total of all alternatives. Since yam (₦50,000) earns more than cassava (₦45,000), yam is the next best alternative, so it is the correct opportunity cost of choosing maize.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na only the one option wey be number two best, e no be all the remaining options add together. Since yam (₦50,000) pass cassava (₦45,000), na yam be the next best option, so na im be the correct opportunity cost of choosing maize.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes scarcity from a shortage?
o: Scarcity is the general and permanent limitation of resources compared to unlimited wants, while a shortage is a temporary lack of supply at the prevailing price
Scarcity affects only developing countries while shortage affects only developed countries
Shortage is a permanent condition while scarcity is only temporary
Scarcity and shortage mean exactly the same thing in economics
questions.e: Scarcity is a permanent, universal economic problem affecting every country regardless of wealth, while a shortage is a short-term situation, such as when fuel is temporarily unavailable at the pump price. The other options wrongly treat the two terms as identical or get the permanence reversed.
questions.p: Scarcity na permanent problem wey dey everywhere, e no dey choose rich or poor country, but shortage na short-time matter, like when fuel no dey available for the pump price for some days. The other options don mix up the two terms wrongly.

questions.q: The ages (in years) of 5 pupils in a Lagos primary school club are: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. What is the mean age of the pupils?
questions.e: Mean = sum of values divided by number of values. Sum = 4+6+8+10+12 = 40, and 40 divided by 5 = 8.
questions.p: Mean na when you add all the numbers togeda den divide by how many dem be. 4+6+8+10+12 give 40, 40 divide by 5 na 8.

questions.q: In statistics, which measure of central tendency is defined as the value that occurs most frequently in a set of data?
questions.e: The mode is the value that appears most often in a data set. The mean is the average, the median is the middle value, and the range measures spread, not central tendency.
questions.p: Mode na di value wey dey show pass for inside data. Mean na average, median na di middle number, range na di spread, dem no be mode.

questions.q: A table shows the prices of goods at Oja Oba market in one morning: Yam costs ₦500, Rice costs ₦700, Beans costs ₦600, Garri costs ₦300, and Maize costs ₦400. Based on this table, which commodity has the highest price?
questions.e: Comparing the prices listed, Rice at ₦700 is higher than Yam (₦500), Beans (₦600), Garri (₦300) and Maize (₦400). So Rice has the highest price.
questions.p: If you compare di prices for di table, Rice na ₦700, e pass Yam (₦500), Beans (₦600), Garri (₦300) and Maize (₦400). So Rice get di highest price.

questions.q: In a test, the scores of 10 students and their frequencies are: score 3 (2 students), score 5 (3 students), score 7 (4 students), score 9 (1 student). What is the mean score?
questions.e: Multiply each score by its frequency and add: (3x2)+(5x3)+(7x4)+(9x1) = 6+15+28+9 = 58. Divide by total number of students, 10, to get 58/10 = 5.8.
questions.p: Multiply each score by im frequency den add dem: (3x2)+(5x3)+(7x4)+(9x1) = 6+15+28+9 = 58. Divide 58 by 10 students, you go get 5.8.

questions.q: In Economics, demand for a commodity means:
o: the desire to own a commodity regardless of price
the quantity of a commodity a producer is willing to sell
the willingness and ability of a consumer to buy a commodity at a given price
the total stock of a commodity available in the market
questions.e: Demand is not just wanting something; it must be backed by the ability (money) and willingness to pay for it at a particular price. This makes option C the correct economic meaning of demand.
questions.p: Demand no just mean say you wan buy something. You must get money and also willing to pay for am for that price. Na so economics take explain demand, so C correct.

questions.q: According to the law of demand, if the price of garri falls while other factors remain constant, the quantity of garri demanded will:
questions.e: The law of demand states that price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions, so a fall in price normally leads to a rise in quantity demanded, other things being equal.
questions.p: Law of demand talk say price and quantity demanded dey move for opposite direction. If price fall, people go wan buy more, so quantity demanded go increase.

questions.q: The demand for bricklayers in Lagos tends to rise whenever there is an increase in building construction activities. This situation best illustrates:
questions.e: Derived demand occurs when the demand for one good or service depends on the demand for another good it helps to produce. Bricklayers are demanded because of the demand for buildings, so their demand is 'derived' from building construction.
questions.p: Derived demand na when demand for one thing dey depend on demand for another thing. Bricklayers dey needed because people wan build house, so na from building construction dem get their demand. B correct.

questions.q: The price of a bag of garri in Mile 12 market increased from ₦2,000 to ₦2,400 per bag. As a result, the quantity demanded per week fell from 50 bags to 40 bags. Using the percentage method, calculate the price elasticity of demand (ignore the negative sign).
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity demanded = (40-50)/50 = -20%. Percentage change in price = (2400-2000)/2000 = 20%. Elasticity = 20%/20% = 1.0, meaning demand is unit elastic.
questions.p: Quantity demanded change by -20% (from 50 to 40), price also change by 20% (from 2000 to 2400). Divide the two percentages, you go get 1.0, na unit elastic demand.

questions.q: Garri is the main staple food for many low-income families in a certain community. When the price of garri falls sharply, some of these families actually buy less garri because their real income rises enough for them to afford better foods like rice and beans instead. This behaviour, which contradicts the normal law of demand, best describes garri as:
questions.e: A Giffen good is a special inferior good where quantity demanded falls when price falls, because the resulting rise in real income makes consumers switch to better substitutes. This is the exact situation described for garri, so it is a Giffen good.
questions.p: Giffen good na special kind inferior good wey when price fall, people go buy am less, because their real money don increase well-well make dem fit buy better food like rice. Na so e happen for garri here, so B correct.

questions.q: The demand schedule for oranges in a local market shows: at ₦25 per orange, 80 oranges are demanded per day; at ₦30 per orange, 60 oranges are demanded per day. Using the percentage method, calculate the price elasticity of demand between these two prices (ignore the negative sign).
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity demanded = (60-80)/80 = -25%. Percentage change in price = (30-25)/25 = 20%. Elasticity = 25%/20% = 1.25, so demand is elastic (greater than 1).
questions.p: Quantity demanded change by -25% (from 80 to 60), price change by 20% (from 25 to 30). When you divide 25% by 20%, you go get 1.25, demand na elastic one.

questions.q: In Economics, supply refers to which of the following?
o: The quantity of a commodity that producers are willing and able to offer for sale at a given price within a particular period
The stock of unsold goods kept in a trader's warehouse
The quantity of a commodity that consumers desire to purchase at a given price
The total quantity of goods produced by a country in a year
questions.e: Supply is about sellers, not buyers or warehouse stock. It must involve both willingness and ability to sell at a stated price over a time period.
questions.p: Supply na about sellers, no be buyers or goods wey dey warehouse. E must involve say seller wan sell and fit sell am for one particular price within one period.

questions.q: The law of supply states that, other things being equal, as the price of a commodity rises, the quantity supplied of that commodity will:
questions.e: The law of supply shows a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied: higher price encourages producers to supply more because it is more profitable.
questions.p: Law of supply talk say price and quantity supplied dey waka together: if price go up, sellers go wan supply more because profit go sweet them.

questions.q: Which of the following will most likely lead to an increase in the supply of cassava in Oyo State?
o: An increase in the price of fertilizer used by farmers
An outbreak of army worm attack on cassava farms
An increase in tax imposed on cassava farmers
The discovery of a new high-yielding cassava variety by farmers
questions.e: A high-yielding variety means farmers can harvest more cassava from the same land and inputs, directly increasing supply. The other options (higher input cost, pest attack, higher tax) all reduce supply.
questions.p: If farmers get better cassava type wey dey yield well, dem go harvest pass before for the same land, so supply go increase. The other options go reduce supply because dem go raise cost or spoil farm.

questions.q: Mrs. Adaeze, a tomato seller at Mile 12 market, offers more baskets of tomatoes for sale when the price rises from ₦200 to ₦300 per basket, while all other factors remain constant. This situation best illustrates a:
o: shift of the supply curve to the right
shift of the supply curve to the left
questions.e: Since only the price changed (other factors stayed the same), the change in quantity supplied is shown as a movement along the existing supply curve, not a shift.
questions.p: Na only price change, other things no change, so the change for quantity wey she supply na movement for the same supply curve, e no be shift.

questions.q: The price of a bag of rice increased from ₦28,000 to ₦32,000. As a result, a trader's weekly supply of rice increased from 50 bags to 60 bags. What is the price elasticity of supply?
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity = (10/50) x 100 = 20%. Percentage change in price = (4000/28000) x 100 = 14.3%. Elasticity = 20/14.3 = 1.4.
questions.p: Percentage change for quantity = (10/50) x 100 = 20%. Percentage change for price = (4000/28000) x 100 = 14.3%. Elasticity = 20 divide by 14.3 = 1.4.

questions.q: If the coefficient of price elasticity of supply of a commodity is calculated to be 0.6, the supply of the commodity is said to be:
questions.e: Any elasticity coefficient less than 1 means that quantity supplied changes proportionately less than price, which is called inelastic supply.
questions.p: If the elasticity number dey less pass 1, e mean say the quantity wey dem supply no dey change well-well pass the price change, dem dey call am inelastic.

questions.q: The supply function for a commodity is given as Qs = -20 + 5P, where Qs is the quantity supplied in units per week and P is the price in naira per unit. What is the minimum price at which producers will be willing to supply the commodity (that is, when Qs = 0)?
questions.e: Set Qs = 0: 0 = -20 + 5P, so 5P = 20, giving P = 4. Below this price, producers are not willing to supply any unit of the commodity.
questions.p: Make Qs = 0: 0 = -20 + 5P, so 5P = 20, P go be 4. If price dey below 4, producers no go wan supply the commodity at all.

questions.q: In Economics, what does 'price elasticity of demand' measure?
o: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of the good
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in consumers' income
The responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in the price of the good
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of a related good
questions.e: Price elasticity of demand (PED) shows how much the quantity demanded of a good changes when its own price changes. The other options describe elasticity of supply, income elasticity and cross elasticity respectively.
questions.p: Price elasticity of demand na how quantity wey people dey demand for one good go change if di price of dat same good change. Di oda options na for supply, income and cross elasticity, no be price elasticity of demand.

questions.q: The price of a tuber of yam in Oyingbo market rises from ₦500 to ₦600. This leads to an increase in quantity supplied from 150 tubers to 180 tubers per week. Calculate the coefficient of price elasticity of supply.
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity supplied = (180-150)/150 x 100 = 20%. Percentage change in price = (600-500)/500 x 100 = 20%. Elasticity of supply = 20/20 = 1.0, which is unitary elastic.
questions.p: Quantity wey dem supply change be (180-150)/150 x 100 = 20%. Price change be (600-500)/500 x 100 = 20%. So elasticity = 20/20 = 1.0, na unitary elastic.

questions.q: A demand curve is drawn as a straight vertical line, showing that no matter how the price of the good changes, the quantity demanded stays exactly the same. What type of demand does this represent?
questions.e: A vertical demand curve means quantity demanded does not change at all when price changes, which is the definition of perfectly inelastic demand. This gives a price elasticity coefficient of zero.
questions.p: If di demand curve dey stand straight up and down, e mean say quantity wey people wan buy no dey change at all even if price change. Dat one na perfectly inelastic demand, elasticity be zero.

questions.q: Which of the following goods is likely to have the most inelastic demand among people in Nigeria?
questions.e: Table salt is a basic necessity with no close substitute and takes a small share of income, so people keep buying almost the same amount even when its price changes. The other goods are luxuries with substitutes, making their demand more elastic.
questions.p: Salt na necessity wey no get substitute and e no cost plenty for person pocket, so people go still buy am even if price change small. Di oda tins na luxury wey get substitutes, so dem go dey elastic pass salt.

questions.q: The price of tea increases by 10%. As a result, the quantity demanded of coffee (a substitute good) increases by 15%. Calculate the coefficient of cross elasticity of demand between tea and coffee.
questions.e: Cross elasticity of demand = percentage change in quantity demanded of coffee divided by percentage change in price of tea = 15/10 = 1.5. The positive value confirms that tea and coffee are substitute goods, as expected.
questions.p: Cross elasticity = percentage wey quantity of coffee change divide by percentage wey price of tea change = 15/10 = 1.5. Di positive answer show say tea and coffee na substitute goods.

questions.q: Mrs Okafor's monthly income rises from ₦40,000 to ₦50,000. As a result, her demand for rice increases from 20kg to 24kg per month. Calculate the coefficient of income elasticity of demand for rice.
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity demanded = (24-20)/20 x 100 = 20%. Percentage change in income = (50000-40000)/40000 x 100 = 25%. Income elasticity = 20/25 = 0.8, a positive value less than 1, showing rice is a normal necessity good.
questions.p: Quantity wey demand change be (24-20)/20 x 100 = 20%. Income change be (50000-40000)/40000 x 100 = 25%. Income elasticity = 20/25 = 0.8, na positive but e small pass 1, so rice na normal necessity good.

questions.q: In economics, the equilibrium price of a commodity such as yam in Oja Oba market is best described as:
o: The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
The price at which total supply exceeds total demand
The highest price a producer can charge
The price fixed by government for all goods
questions.e: Equilibrium price is where the quantity buyers want to buy equals the quantity sellers want to sell. At this price, there is no shortage or surplus in the market.
questions.p: Equilibrium price na di price wey wetin buyer wan buy match wetin seller wan sell. For dis price, shortage or surplus no dey.

questions.q: The demand for a bag of beans in Dawanau market is given as Qd = 90 - 3P, while the supply is given as Qs = 10 + 2P, where P is the price in naira and Q is the quantity in bags. What is the equilibrium price?
questions.e: At equilibrium, Qd = Qs, so 90 - 3P = 10 + 2P. Collecting like terms gives 80 = 5P, so P = 16.
questions.p: For equilibrium, Qd and Qs go dey equal: 90 - 3P = 10 + 2P. If you arrange am, 80 = 5P, so P = 16.

questions.q: The demand function for fresh tomatoes at Mile 12 market is Qd = 60 - 2P, and the supply function is Qs = 10 + 3P, where P is price in naira per basket and Q is quantity of baskets. What is the equilibrium quantity of tomatoes sold?
questions.e: Setting Qd = Qs gives 60 - 2P = 10 + 3P, so 50 = 5P and P = 10. Substituting P = 10 into Qd = 60 - 2P gives Q = 60 - 20 = 40 baskets.
questions.p: Make Qd equal Qs: 60 - 2P = 10 + 3P, e give 50 = 5P, so P = 10. Put P = 10 inside Qd = 60 - 2P, e go give Q = 40 baskets.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes price control as used in economics?
o: The practice of allowing prices to rise without any limit
The free interaction of demand and supply forces
A method used by producers to maximize profit without government interference
A government policy of fixing prices by law instead of leaving them to market forces
questions.e: Price control happens when government, by law, sets the price of a good or service instead of allowing demand and supply to determine it freely.
questions.p: Price control na when government use law fix price of goods or service, instead make demand and supply dey decide am by demself.

questions.q: If the government fixes a minimum price for a bag of garri at Mile 12 market that is above the market equilibrium price, what is the most likely immediate effect?
o: Demand for garri increases sharply above supply
Shortage of garri in the market
The equilibrium price remains completely unchanged
Surplus of garri as quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
questions.e: A minimum price set above equilibrium encourages sellers to supply more while buyers demand less at that higher price, so quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, creating a surplus.
questions.p: When minimum price pass equilibrium, sellers go wan sell plenty but buyers go buy small for dat high price, so wetin dem supply go pass wetin dem demand, dat one na surplus.

questions.q: The demand for a crate of eggs in Garki market is Qd = 80 - 2P, and the supply is Qs = 20 + 2P, where P is price in naira and Q is quantity of crates. Government fixes a minimum price of ₦20 per crate, which is above the equilibrium price. What is the size of the surplus created at this fixed price?
questions.e: At P = 20, Qs = 20 + 2(20) = 60 and Qd = 80 - 2(20) = 40. Surplus = Qs - Qd = 60 - 40 = 20 crates, since more is supplied than demanded at the higher fixed price.
questions.p: If P = 20, Qs = 20 + 2(20) = 60 and Qd = 80 - 2(20) = 40. Surplus na Qs minus Qd = 60 - 40 = 20 crates, because supply pass demand for dat high price.

questions.q: The Lagos State Government fixes the maximum price of a bag of rice at ₦25,000, which is below the market equilibrium price of ₦32,000. Which of the following is LEAST likely to happen as a result of this policy?
o: Emergence of a black market where rice is sold above ₦25,000
Producers increasing the quantity of rice supplied at ₦25,000
Shortage of rice at the official price
questions.e: Since ₦25,000 is below equilibrium, producers earn less profit and will reduce, not increase, the quantity supplied, while buyers still want more at the low price. This mismatch causes shortages, queues and black markets, but an increase in supply by producers is not realistic.
questions.p: Because ₦25,000 dey below equilibrium, producers go gain small profit, so dem go reduce quantity wey dem dey supply, no be increase am, while buyers still wan buy plenty for di cheap price. Dis one go cause shortage, queue and black market, but producers no fit increase supply for dat low price.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four factors of production recognized in Economics?
questions.e: Economics recognizes four factors of production: land, labour, capital and entrepreneur. Money is not itself a factor; it is only used as a medium of exchange to acquire the real factors of production.
questions.p: Economics get only four factors: land, labour, capital and entrepreneur. Money no be factor, na just wetin dem dey use buy the real factors.

questions.q: In Economics, which factor payment is given to the entrepreneur for organizing the other factors of production and bearing business risk?
questions.e: Profit is the reward for entrepreneurship because the entrepreneur takes risks and coordinates land, labour and capital. Rent is for land, wage for labour, and interest for capital.
questions.p: Profit na wetin entrepreneur dey collect because e dey carry risk and arrange the other factors. Rent na for land, wage na for labour, interest na for capital.

questions.q: A cocoa farmer in Ondo State has a fixed 4-hectare farmland. He hires workers one at a time and records the following total output in bags of cocoa: 1 worker = 8 bags, 2 workers = 18 bags, 3 workers = 26 bags, 4 workers = 30 bags, 5 workers = 30 bags. At which number of workers does the law of diminishing returns begin to set in (that is, where marginal product first starts to fall)?
questions.e: The marginal product (extra bags per extra worker) is 8, 10, 8, 4, 0 for workers 1 to 5. It rises from the 1st to the 2nd worker (8 to 10) then falls from the 3rd worker (10 to 8), so diminishing returns set in at the 3rd worker.
questions.p: Extra bags wey each new worker add na 8, 10, 8, 4, 0. E rise from first to second worker (8 to 10) then e begin fall from the 3rd worker (10 to 8), so diminishing returns start from the 3rd worker.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'division of labour' in a production process?
o: Combining all production tasks into one worker's job
Sharing profit equally among all the workers
Rotating workers regularly to prevent them from specializing
Breaking down a production process into separate tasks performed by different workers
questions.e: Division of labour means splitting a production process into smaller tasks so that different workers specialize in each part, which increases efficiency and total output.
questions.p: Division of labour mean say dem go break the work process into small small parts make different worker specialize for each part, dis one dey increase efficiency and output.

questions.q: A palm oil factory's total product is 48 units when 6 workers are employed, and 42 units when 5 workers are employed. What is the marginal product of the 6th worker?
questions.e: Marginal product = change in total product / change in number of workers = (48 - 42) / (6 - 5) = 6. So the 6th worker added 6 extra units to total output.
questions.p: Marginal product = change for total product divide by change for worker = (48 - 42) / 1 = 6. So the 6th worker add 6 extra units.

questions.q: Which stage of production involves converting raw materials, such as cotton, into finished goods, such as clothes?
questions.e: Secondary production is the stage where raw materials are processed or manufactured into finished or semi-finished goods, such as turning cotton into clothes. Primary production deals with extraction, while tertiary production covers services.
questions.p: Secondary production na when dem process raw materials turn am to finished goods, like cotton to clothes. Primary na extraction, tertiary na services.

questions.q: In the theory of production, which statement correctly describes the 'long run' period for a firm?
o: The firm can vary labour only while land stays fixed
The firm can vary land and capital only while labour stays fixed
The firm cannot vary any factor of production at all
The firm can vary all its factors of production, including land and capital
questions.e: In the long run, a firm has enough time to change all its factors of production, including land and capital, unlike in the short run where at least one factor (often land or capital) remains fixed.
questions.p: For long run, firm get enough time to change all im factors of production, including land and capital, unlike short run where one factor (land or capital) go still dey fixed.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a FIXED cost to a small garment-making business in Onitsha?
o: Wages of tailors paid per piece of cloth sewn
Cost of fabric used for sewing
questions.e: Fixed cost does not change with the level of output in the short run. Rent must be paid whether the firm sews many clothes or none at all, unlike fabric, wages per piece and thread which rise as output rises.
questions.p: Fixed cost na cost wey no dey change even if the factory produce plenty or small. Rent na im dey constant like that, but fabric, wages-per-piece and thread go dey increase as production increase.

questions.q: Total revenue of a firm is best described as:
o: Total fixed cost plus total variable cost
Price per unit minus average cost of production
Price per unit multiplied by the quantity of goods sold
Total cost divided by the quantity produced
questions.e: Total revenue (TR) is the income a firm earns from sales, calculated as Price x Quantity Sold. The other options describe profit margin, total cost and average cost respectively, not total revenue.
questions.p: Total revenue na the money wey the business get from selling, e be Price multiply by the Quantity wey dem sell. The other options dey talk about profit, total cost and average cost, no be total revenue.

questions.q: A palm-oil processor produces 50 litres of oil at a total cost of ₦15,000. What is the average cost of production per litre?
questions.e: Average cost = Total cost / Quantity produced = 15000/50 = ₦300. The other options come from wrong division of the figures given.
questions.p: Average cost = Total cost divide by Quantity, so na 15000/50 = ₦300. The other answers na from wrong division of the numbers.

questions.q: A bakery's total cost of producing 10 loaves of bread is ₦2,000. When it produces 11 loaves, total cost rises to ₦2,250. What is the marginal cost of the 11th loaf?
questions.e: Marginal cost is the extra cost of producing one more unit: MC = Change in Total Cost / Change in Quantity = (2250 - 2000)/(11 - 10) = ₦250.
questions.p: Marginal cost na the extra cost wey dem spend to produce one more unit: (2250 - 2000)/(11-10) = ₦250.

questions.q: Mallam Yusuf sells 200 bags of rice at ₦1,500 per bag. His total cost of buying and transporting the rice was ₦250,000. What was his total profit?
questions.e: Total revenue = 200 x 1500 = ₦300,000. Profit = Total revenue - Total cost = 300,000 - 250,000 = ₦50,000.
questions.p: Total revenue = 200 x 1500 = ₦300,000. Profit = Total revenue minus Total cost = 300,000 - 250,000 = ₦50,000.

questions.q: A soap-making company has a total fixed cost of ₦40,000. Each unit of soap sells for ₦400 and costs ₦200 to produce as variable cost. How many units must the company sell to break even?
questions.e: Break-even quantity = Fixed cost / (Price per unit - Variable cost per unit) = 40000/(400-200) = 40000/200 = 200 units. At this point total revenue equals total cost, so there is no profit or loss.
questions.p: Break-even quantity = Fixed cost divide by (Price minus Variable cost per unit) = 40000/(400-200) = 200 units. Na the point wey total revenue go balance total cost, no profit no loss.

questions.q: A trader selling bags of garri notices that when the price is ₦50 per bag, he sells 10 bags, giving total revenue of ₦500. When he reduces the price to ₦48 per bag, he sells 11 bags, giving total revenue of ₦528. What is the marginal revenue of the 11th bag sold?
questions.e: Marginal revenue is the extra revenue from selling one more unit: MR = Change in Total Revenue / Change in Quantity = (528 - 500)/(11 - 10) = ₦28. Note MR is less than the new price of ₦48 because the price cut applies to all units sold, not just the extra one.
questions.p: Marginal revenue na the extra money wey dem get from selling one more bag: (528-500)/(11-10) = ₦28. E dey less than the new price of ₦48 because the price wey e reduce apply to all the bags, no be only the extra one.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a market structure where there are many buyers and sellers of a homogeneous (identical) product, with freedom of entry and exit for firms?
questions.e: Perfect competition is a market with many buyers and sellers selling identical goods, and firms can enter or leave the market freely. No single firm can influence the price because each one is too small.
questions.p: Perfect competition na market wey get plenty buyer and seller wey dey sell the same kind product, and any company fit enter or comot anytime. No single company fit control the price because dem too small.

questions.q: A market situation where a single firm is the sole producer of a commodity that has no close substitute is known as:
questions.e: Monopoly exists when only one firm controls the entire supply of a product and there is no close substitute, so the firm has full control over price and output.
questions.p: Monopoly na when one company alone dey control the whole supply of one product and no other product fit replace am. Na only that company dey fix the price and how much e go produce.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of an oligopolistic market such as the Nigerian telecommunications industry with a few dominant network providers?
o: Firms are interdependent in their pricing and output decisions
There are no barriers to entry
Price is determined by market forces alone
questions.e: In oligopoly, because few large firms dominate the market, any pricing or output decision by one firm directly affects the others, so firms watch and react to each other's actions. This mutual dependence is called interdependence.
questions.p: For oligopoly, na few big companies dey control the market, so if one company change price or wetin e dey produce, e go affect the others. Dis kain connection na wetin dem call interdependence.

questions.q: Under perfect competition, a single firm is described as a 'price taker' mainly because:
o: There is only one firm supplying the whole market
The firm's output is too small to influence the market price
The firm fixes its own price to maximize profit
The government controls the price of the product
questions.e: Since there are many small firms in perfect competition, each firm's output is a tiny fraction of total market supply. No single firm can raise or lower the market price by changing its own output, so each firm simply accepts (takes) the price set by the market.
questions.p: Because plenty small company dey for perfect competition, one company output no reach change the market price at all. So each company just dey accept the price wey the market set, na why dem call am 'price taker'.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a natural barrier to entry that can give rise to monopoly power?
o: Government subsidy given equally to all new firms
High level of competition among many sellers
Free advertising offered by the firm to attract customers
Exclusive ownership or control of a key raw material needed for production
questions.e: A natural barrier to entry occurs when one firm has sole control of a vital resource, such as a rare mineral deposit, which prevents other firms from entering the industry and competing. This gives the controlling firm monopoly power.
questions.p: Natural barrier to entry na when one company alone get control over important raw material, like rare mineral, so other company no fit enter the business to compete. Dis one go give the company monopoly power.

questions.q: In a certain industry, five firms share the market as follows: Firm P = 30%, Firm Q = 20%, Firm R = 25%, Firm S = 15%, Firm T = 10%. What is the four-firm concentration ratio (the combined market share of the four largest firms)?
questions.e: Arrange the shares from highest to lowest: P=30%, R=25%, Q=20%, S=15%, T=10%. The four largest are P, R, Q and S, so the four-firm concentration ratio = 30+25+20+15 = 90%.
questions.p: Arrange the shares from biggest to smallest: P=30%, R=25%, Q=20%, S=15%, T=10%. The four biggest na P, R, Q and S, so the four-firm concentration ratio = 30+25+20+15 = 90%.

questions.q: The kinked demand curve theory in economics is mainly used to explain why firms in an oligopolistic market tend to:
o: Produce at the lowest possible cost always
Earn zero economic profit in the long run
Keep their prices stable once set, fearing how rivals will react
Always change prices frequently to attract customers
questions.e: The kinked demand curve theory shows that if an oligopolist raises its price, rivals will not follow, so it loses many customers; but if it lowers its price, rivals will match it, so it gains little. This makes firms prefer to keep prices stable rather than risk a price war.
questions.p: Kinked demand curve theory show say if oligopolist increase price, im rival no go follow am, so e go lose plenty customer; but if e reduce price, rival go follow am reduce theirs too, so e no go gain plenty. Na why most of dem prefer to leave price steady instead of start price war.

questions.q: Which type of business organisation is owned, managed and controlled by one person who provides all the capital, takes all the decisions and bears all the risks alone?
questions.e: A sole proprietorship is owned by a single individual who supplies the capital, makes all decisions and takes all the profit or loss alone. Partnership, companies and cooperatives all involve more than one owner.
questions.p: Sole proprietorship na business wey one person dey own, dey manage and dey carry all the risk by imself. Partnership, companies and cooperative get plenty owners.

questions.q: Which document of a registered company contains the internal rules that guide how the company's daily affairs, meetings and voting rights of members should be conducted?
questions.e: The Articles of Association deals with the internal management of the company, such as rules for meetings and voting. The Memorandum of Association, on the other hand, defines the company's relationship with outsiders, such as its objectives and name.
questions.p: Articles of Association na the paper wey carry the internal rules wey dey guide how the company go run im meetings and voting. Memorandum of Association na for outside matter like company name and aim.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a public limited company from a private limited company in Nigeria?
o: Both can only raise capital by borrowing from banks
Only a public limited company can sue and be sued in court
A private limited company must have more than fifty shareholders
Shares of a public limited company can be offered for sale to the general public through the stock exchange, unlike those of a private limited company
questions.e: A major distinguishing feature is that a public limited company (Plc) can sell its shares to the general public through the stock exchange, while a private limited company (Ltd) restricts share transfer to a small group of people. Both types can sue and be sued, since both have corporate personality.
questions.p: The main difference be say public limited company (Plc) fit sell im shares to everybody through stock exchange, but private limited company (Ltd) no fit do dat one; dem dey restrict am. Both of dem fit sue and dem fit sue dem too.

questions.q: What is the main aim of a consumer cooperative society formed by workers in a market like Oja-Oba?
o: To raise large capital by selling shares to the public on the stock exchange
To give loans only to people who are not members of the society
To buy goods in bulk directly from producers and sell to members at fair, affordable prices
To maximise profit for a few wealthy shareholders
questions.e: A consumer cooperative society exists mainly to buy goods in large quantities at cheaper rates and resell them to its members at fair prices, cutting out middlemen. It is not focused on profit maximisation for shareholders like a company.
questions.p: Consumer cooperative society dey buy things plenty-plenty for cheap price, then dem go resell am to members for fair price, so dem go avoid middleman wahala. E no be like company wey dey focus on making profit for shareholders.

questions.q: Adaeze Traders Plc declared a total dividend of ₦450,000 for the year. If the company has 15,000 ordinary shares in issue, what is the dividend paid per share?
questions.e: Dividend per share is total dividend divided by number of shares: ₦450,000 ÷ 15,000 = ₦30 per share. This shows how much each shareholder earns for every share they hold.
questions.p: To find dividend per share, you go divide the total dividend by the number of shares: ₦450,000 ÷ 15,000 = ₦30 per share. Na so much each shareholder go collect for every share wey dem hold.

questions.q: Why would an entrepreneur planning a large, capital-intensive business prefer to register as a private limited liability company rather than operate as a sole proprietor?
o: Because a sole proprietorship needs more start-up capital than a limited company
Because a private limited company pays less tax than a sole proprietorship
Because a private limited company is not required to keep financial records
Because the liability of a private limited company is limited to the amount invested, so the owner's personal property is protected if the business fails
questions.e: In a private limited company, the owners (shareholders) only lose the money they invested if the business fails, because the company has a separate legal identity. A sole proprietor has unlimited liability, meaning personal property can be seized to pay business debts, which makes a limited company safer for a risky, capital-intensive venture.
questions.p: For private limited company, the owners go only lose the money wey dem put inside if business scatter, because company get im own separate legal identity. Sole proprietor get unlimited liability, so dem fit use im personal property pay business debt, dat na why limited company safer for big risky business.

questions.q: In Nigeria, the official exercise carried out periodically to count and record the number of people living in the country, along with details such as their age, sex and occupation, is called the:
questions.e: A population census is the official counting and recording of all people in a country at a given time, including facts such as age, sex and occupation. Density, labour force survey and projection are different concepts.
questions.p: Population census na when government dey count and write down everybody for di kontri, including dia age, sex and work. E no be di same thing as density, labour force survey or projection.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the labour force of a country?
o: All persons of working age (15-64 years) who are either employed or actively seeking work
Only those workers employed in the formal, salaried sector
All persons living in the country, including children and the aged
Retired persons who still do occasional part-time jobs
questions.e: The labour force consists of working-age people who are employed plus those unemployed but actively looking for work. The other options wrongly include non-working groups or wrongly exclude job seekers.
questions.p: Labour force na people wey dey working age (15-64 years) wey dey work or dey find work. Di oda options include pikin and old people wey no suppose dey counted, or dem too narrow di meaning.

questions.q: The town of Isiama has a total population of 450,000 people and covers a land area of 1,500 square kilometres. Calculate the population density of the town.
questions.e: Population density = total population ÷ land area = 450,000 ÷ 1,500 = 300 persons per km^2.
questions.p: Density na population divide by area: 450,000 ÷ 1,500 = 300 persons per km^2.

questions.q: In a certain year, the birth rate of a country was 35 per 1,000 people and the death rate was 15 per 1,000 people. Calculate the country's natural rate of population growth for that year.
questions.e: Natural growth rate = (birth rate - death rate) ÷ 1,000 × 100 = (35-15) ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 2%. This excludes migration and only considers births and deaths.
questions.p: Natural growth rate na (birth rate minus death rate) divide 1000 times 100: (35-15) ÷ 1000 × 100 = 2%. Migration no dey included, na only birth and death.

questions.q: A country's population is said to have grown beyond its optimum level when a further increase in population causes:
o: Total output to increase while average output (income) per head begins to fall
Both total output and average output per head to rise together
The labour force participation rate to increase steadily
The dependency ratio to fall below 20%
questions.e: Optimum population is the level at which output per head is highest. Beyond this point, more people cause average income per head to fall even though total output may still rise, because resources are fixed. The other options do not describe this situation of overpopulation.
questions.p: Optimum population na di level wey average income per head dey highest. If population pass dis level, average income per head go begin fall even as total output still dey rise, because resources no dey increase same way. B, C and D no match dis explanation.

questions.q: In a certain state, the working-age population (15-64 years) is 2,000,000. Out of this number, 1,200,000 people are either employed or actively seeking jobs, while the rest are full-time students, homemakers or persons who have given up looking for work. Calculate the labour force participation rate of the state.
questions.e: Labour force participation rate = (labour force ÷ working-age population) × 100 = 1,200,000 ÷ 2,000,000 × 100 = 60%. This shows the proportion of the working-age population that is economically active.
questions.p: Labour force participation rate na (labour force divide working-age population) times 100 = 1,200,000 ÷ 2,000,000 × 100 = 60%. Na im dey show how many working-age pesin dey economically active.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains the 'store of value' function of money?
o: It allows goods and services to be exchanged without barter
It enables individuals to keep wealth for future use without it losing value quickly
It serves as a common measure for expressing the price of goods
It allows debts to be settled at a future date
questions.e: Money acts as a store of value when people can save it today and use it later without the value disappearing (unlike perishable goods). Option A describes medium of exchange, C describes measure of value, and D describes standard for deferred payment.
questions.p: Money dey work as store of value when person fit keep am today still use am tomorrow without e dey spoil like food. Option A na medium of exchange, C na measure of value, D na standard for deferred payment.

questions.q: A situation in an economy where there is a persistent and continuous rise in the general price level of goods and services, causing the purchasing power of money to fall, is called:
questions.e: Inflation is defined exactly as a persistent rise in the general price level, which reduces how much goods and services ₦1 can buy. Deflation is the opposite (falling prices), disinflation is a slowdown in the inflation rate, and stagflation combines inflation with stagnant growth.
questions.p: Inflation na when prices dey rise well-well for long time, so money no fit buy as e used to buy before. Deflation na when prices dey fall, disinflation na when inflation dey slow down, stagflation na when inflation dey mix with slow economic growth.

questions.q: Using the quantity theory of money formula MV = PT, where M = money supply, V = velocity of circulation of money, P = general price level, and T = total number of transactions: In an economy, the money supply is ₦3,000,000, the velocity of circulation is 4, and the total number of transactions carried out in a year is 600,000. What is the general price level (P)?
questions.e: From MV = PT, P = MV/T. So P = (3,000,000 x 4) / 600,000 = 12,000,000 / 600,000 = 20. The other options come from dividing or multiplying the wrong numbers.
questions.p: From MV = PT, we fit find P as MV/T. So P = (3,000,000 x 4) / 600,000 = 12,000,000 / 600,000 = 20. Di oda answers na from wrong calculation.

questions.q: Which of the following groups is most likely to benefit during a period of persistent inflation in an economy?
o: Pensioners living on a fixed monthly pension
Workers whose wages are fixed by long-term contracts
Debtors who borrowed money before the inflation started
Savers who keep their money in fixed deposit accounts
questions.e: During inflation, the value of money falls, so debtors repay their loans with money that is worth less than when they borrowed it, which benefits them. Pensioners, fixed-wage workers, and savers with fixed deposits all suffer because their fixed incomes or savings buy less as prices rise.
questions.p: For inflation time, money value dey fall, so debtors go pay back their loan with money wey no cost reach wetin dem borrow — na so dem dey gain. Pensioners, fixed wage workers and savers with fixed deposit go suffer because their fixed money no go fit buy plenty tin again.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes deflation from disinflation?
o: Deflation is a rise in the general price level while disinflation is a fall in the general price level
Deflation means prices and inflation are both rising rapidly, while disinflation means they are both rising slowly
Deflation is a persistent fall in the general price level, while disinflation is simply a slowdown in the rate at which prices are rising
Deflation and disinflation both refer to the same continuous fall in the general price level of goods
questions.e: Deflation occurs when the general price level actually falls over time, while disinflation means prices are still rising but at a slower rate than before (inflation is reducing, not reversing). Option A reverses the definitions, and B and D confuse the two concepts as if they were identical or both rising.
questions.p: Deflation na when prices dey really fall for economy, but disinflation na when prices still dey rise but the speed don slow down (inflation rate dey reduce, e no reverse). Option A don mix up di definitions, B and D dey confuse di two words as if na one thing.

questions.q: Which of the following financial institutions in Nigeria has the sole legal right to issue the naira notes and coins?
questions.e: Only the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is legally empowered to print and issue the naira as the national currency. Commercial banks, the stock exchange and NDIC do not issue currency.
questions.p: Na only Central Bank of Nigeria get the power to print naira notes and coins. Other banks like First Bank no fit do am.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a normal function performed by commercial banks?
o: Granting loans and overdrafts to customers
questions.e: Issuing legal tender currency is the exclusive duty of the central bank, not commercial banks. Commercial banks accept deposits, grant loans and keep valuables safe for customers.
questions.p: To print legal tender money na central bank work, commercial bank no dey do am. Commercial bank dey collect deposit, give loan and keep valuables.

questions.q: When the Central Bank of Nigeria provides emergency funds to a commercial bank that is short of cash to meet its customers' withdrawal demands, the central bank is acting as the
questions.e: When the central bank rescues a commercial bank facing a liquidity shortage by lending it money, it is performing the role of lender of last resort, a key central bank function.
questions.p: If central bank help commercial bank wey no get enough cash give am loan, na 'lender of last resort' work e dey do.

questions.q: A financial institution that specializes in granting long-term loans to support agricultural and industrial projects, rather than accepting ordinary current account deposits, is best classified as a
questions.e: Development banks exist mainly to finance long-term agricultural and industrial projects, unlike commercial banks which focus on short-term deposits and loans. The central bank and bureau de change have different main roles.
questions.p: Bank wey dey give long-term loan for farming and industry na development bank, e no be like commercial bank wey dey focus on current account.

questions.q: Chief Okafor deposits ₦50,000 in a savings account that pays simple interest at 6% per annum. How much interest will he earn after 2 years?
questions.e: Simple interest = Principal x Rate x Time / 100 = 50,000 x 6 x 2 / 100 = ₦6,000. This is the standard simple interest formula.
questions.p: Simple interest = Principal x Rate x Time / 100 = 50,000 x 6 x 2 / 100 = 6,000 naira.

questions.q: The Central Bank of Nigeria wants to reduce the volume of money in circulation in order to control rising inflation. Which monetary policy action would best achieve this goal?
o: Increase the cash reserve ratio of commercial banks
Reduce the liquidity ratio of commercial banks
Buy government securities from the public
questions.e: Raising the cash reserve ratio forces commercial banks to keep more of their deposits with the central bank, leaving less money available to lend out, which reduces money supply. The other options would instead increase money supply.
questions.p: If CBN increase cash reserve ratio, banks go keep more money with CBN, so less money go dey available for them to lend out — this one go reduce money wey dey circulate.

questions.q: A Bureau de Change buys US dollars from customers at ₦1,550 per dollar and sells to customers at ₦1,600 per dollar. If Mrs. Bello sells $500 to the Bureau de Change, how much naira will she receive?
questions.e: Since Mrs. Bello is selling dollars to the Bureau de Change, the buying rate of ₦1,550 per dollar applies: 500 x 1,550 = ₦775,000. The selling rate of ₦1,600 is used only when customers buy dollars from the Bureau, not when they sell.
questions.p: Since Mrs. Bello dey sell dollar give Bureau de Change, na the buying rate ₦1,550 go apply: 500 x 1,550 = ₦775,000. ₦1,600 na for when customer wan buy dollar, no be sell.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main methods used to measure national income?
questions.e: National income is measured using the output (product) method, income method and expenditure method. Population method does not exist as a way of calculating national income.
questions.p: Dem dey measure national income with output method, income method and expenditure method. Population method no be one of di correct methods.

questions.q: Gross National Product (GNP) is obtained from Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by:
questions.e: GNP includes the income earned by citizens abroad minus income earned by foreigners within the country, so GNP = GDP + net income from abroad.
questions.p: GNP na GDP plus net income wey citizens dey earn for abroad minus wetin foreigners earn for inside di country. So we dey add net income from abroad to GDP to get GNP.

questions.q: Nigeria's GDP for a particular year was ₦650 billion. In the same year, income earned by Nigerians working abroad was ₦45 billion, while income earned by foreigners working in Nigeria was ₦60 billion. What was Nigeria's GNP for that year?
questions.e: Net income from abroad = 45 - 60 = -15 billion. GNP = GDP + net income from abroad = 650 + (-15) = ₦635 billion.
questions.p: Net income from abroad be 45 minus 60 wey be -15 billion. GNP be GDP plus dat net income: 650 + (-15) = ₦635 billion.

questions.q: A country's Gross National Product (GNP) for a year was ₦800 billion, and the capital consumption allowance (depreciation) for the year was ₦50 billion. What was the country's Net National Product (NNP) for that year?
questions.e: NNP is found by subtracting depreciation from GNP: NNP = GNP - Depreciation = 800 - 50 = ₦750 billion.
questions.p: NNP be GNP minus depreciation: 800 - 50 = ₦750 billion.

questions.q: A country's national income for a given year was ₦2,400,000,000 and its population was 8,000,000 people. What was the per capita income of the country?
questions.e: Per capita income = National income / Population = 2,400,000,000 / 8,000,000 = ₦300. This shows the average income each person would get if national income were shared equally.
questions.p: Per capita income na National income divide by Population: 2,400,000,000 / 8,000,000 = ₦300. Na im be di average money each person go get if dem share national income equally.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State sells raw cassava to a processor for ₦2,000. The processor turns it into garri and sells it to a retailer for ₦5,000. The retailer then sells the garri to the final consumer for ₦7,000. Using the value-added method of calculating national income, what is the total value added along this production chain?
questions.e: Value added at each stage: farmer = ₦2,000 (no inputs), processor = 5,000 - 2,000 = ₦3,000, retailer = 7,000 - 5,000 = ₦2,000. Total value added = 2,000 + 3,000 + 2,000 = ₦7,000, which equals the final selling price, showing that the value-added method avoids double counting.
questions.p: Value wey each person add: farmer = ₦2,000, processor = 5,000 - 2,000 = ₦3,000, retailer = 7,000 - 5,000 = ₦2,000. If you add dem together: 2,000+3,000+2,000 = ₦7,000, na im be di final selling price, e show say value-added method no dey double count.

questions.q: Public finance is best defined as the branch of economics that studies how:
o: individual households budget their monthly income
government raises revenue and spends it to achieve national economic goals
firms decide the price and output that maximise profit
commercial banks create credit for businesses
questions.e: Public finance deals with how government gets money (through taxes, loans, etc.) and how it spends this money to provide services and meet economic objectives. The other options are about households, banks and firms, not government.
questions.p: Public finance na how government dey raise money and spend am to achieve economic goals for the country. The other options talk about house, bank or company, no be government.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a direct tax paid in Nigeria?
questions.e: A direct tax is paid straight by the person or company on whom it is imposed, and its burden cannot be shifted to another person; company income tax fits this. VAT, import duty and excise duty are indirect taxes because their burden can be passed to the final consumer through prices.
questions.p: Direct tax na tax wey the person wey dem charge am must pay am directly, dem no fit shift am. Company income tax be like that. VAT, import duty and excise duty na indirect tax because dem fit add am to price make consumer pay am.

questions.q: A tax system in which the rate of tax rises as a taxpayer's income increases is called:
questions.e: Under a progressive tax system, people with higher income pay a higher percentage of their income as tax, which helps reduce inequality. In a proportional tax, the rate stays the same for everyone, while a regressive tax takes a higher percentage from low-income earners.
questions.p: Progressive tax na the one wey the percentage of tax dey increase as person income dey increase. E dey help reduce gap between rich and poor. Proportional tax na fixed rate for everybody, regressive tax na the one wey dey chop poor pass rich.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Adam Smith's original canons (principles) of taxation?
questions.e: Adam Smith's four canons of taxation are equity, certainty, convenience and economy. Profitability is not one of them, as taxation is meant to raise revenue fairly and efficiently, not to generate profit for government like a business.
questions.p: Adam Smith talk say tax suppose get equity, certainty, convenience and economy. Profitability no dey inside, because tax no be business wey government dey do to make profit.

questions.q: Which of the following is a source of non-tax revenue to the Nigerian government?
o: Royalties paid by oil exploration companies
questions.e: Royalties are payments made by companies for the right to extract natural resources like crude oil; this is revenue the government earns without imposing a tax. Personal income tax, VAT and company income tax are all forms of tax revenue.
questions.p: Royalty na money wey company dey pay government make dem fit dig resources like crude oil; e no be tax. Personal income tax, VAT and company income tax na tax revenue proper.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha sells goods worth ₦15,000 before Value Added Tax (VAT). If VAT is charged at 7.5%, how much will a customer pay in total for the goods?
questions.e: VAT amount = 7.5% of ₦15,000 = ₦1,125. Total price paid = ₦15,000 + ₦1,125 = ₦16,125. This shows VAT is added on top of the original selling price and paid by the final consumer.
questions.p: VAT wey dem go charge = 7.5% of ₦15,000 = ₦1,125. Total wey customer go pay = ₦15,000 + ₦1,125 = ₦16,125. Na consumer dey carry the VAT load for the end.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'balance of trade' for a country?
o: The difference between a country's total exports and total foreign investments
The total value of all goods and services bought and sold by a country in a year
The difference between the value of a country's visible exports and visible imports
The total amount of foreign exchange earned from tourism and shipping services
questions.e: Balance of trade deals only with visible (physical) goods, that is, the value of exported goods minus the value of imported goods. It does not include services or investment flows.
questions.p: Balance of trade na the difference wey dey between the value of goods wey country sell comot (export) and the one wey e bring in (import). E no include services or investment.

questions.q: Which of these transactions is an example of invisible trade for Nigeria?
o: Payment of freight charges to a foreign shipping company
Exportation of crude oil to the United States
Exportation of cocoa beans to the Netherlands
questions.e: Invisible trade involves services rather than physical goods. Paying a foreign shipping company for freight is a service transaction, unlike the export/import of crude oil, rice or cocoa which are visible (physical) goods.
questions.p: Invisible trade na about service, no be physical goods. To pay foreign shipping company for freight na service, but crude oil, rice and cocoa na physical goods wey dem dey export or import.

questions.q: In a particular year, a country exported goods worth ₦620 million and imported goods worth ₦545 million. What was the country's balance of trade, where a positive figure means a surplus and a negative figure means a deficit?
questions.e: Balance of trade = value of exports minus value of imports = 620 - 545 = ₦75 million, which is a surplus because exports exceed imports.
questions.p: Balance of trade na export minus import: 620 - 545 = ₦75 million. Na surplus because export pass import.

questions.q: A country's export price index is 150 while its import price index is 120, with the base year index equal to 100. Calculate the country's terms of trade.
questions.e: Terms of trade = (export price index / import price index) x 100 = (150/120) x 100 = 125. A figure above 100 shows favourable terms of trade for the country.
questions.p: Terms of trade = (export price index / import price index) x 100 = (150/120) x 100 = 125. Since e pass 100, e mean say the terms of trade favour the country.

questions.q: Ghana can produce one tonne of cocoa using fewer resources than Nigeria, while Nigeria can produce one barrel of crude oil using fewer resources than Ghana. If both countries specialise in the good they produce more efficiently and trade with each other, which trade theory is best illustrated?
questions.e: Since each country uses fewer resources to produce one particular good compared to the other country, this is a case of absolute advantage, where each country specialises in the good it produces most efficiently in absolute terms.
questions.p: Because each country dey use less resources to produce one particular good pass the other country, na absolute advantage be dis, where each country go specialise for the good wey e sabi produce best.

questions.q: A country's export price index was 140 in Year 1 but fell to 112 in Year 2, while its import price index was 100 in Year 1 and rose to 112 in Year 2. By how many points did the terms of trade fall between Year 1 and Year 2?
questions.e: Terms of trade Year 1 = (140/100) x 100 = 140. Terms of trade Year 2 = (112/112) x 100 = 100. The fall in terms of trade = 140 - 100 = 40 points, showing the country's trading position worsened.
questions.p: Terms of trade Year 1 = (140/100) x 100 = 140. Terms of trade Year 2 = (112/112) x 100 = 100. The fall na 140 - 100 = 40 points, e mean say the country trading position don bad pass before.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines economic development?
o: A sustained increase in real per capita income accompanied by positive structural and qualitative changes in the economy
An increase in the population of a country within a given year
An increase in the total output of goods and services in a country over time
The total value of goods and services produced in a country within a year
questions.e: Economic development is more than just more output; it means real income per person rises steadily while the structure of the economy, welfare and quality of life also improve. Simple output growth or population increase alone does not amount to development.
questions.p: Economic development no be just say output increase; e mean say income wey dey reach person head dey rise well-well, and the kind of life and structure of economy dey better too. Just population or output increase no be development.

questions.q: What is the major difference between economic growth and economic development?
o: Growth leads to inflation while development leads to deflation
Growth only occurs in developed countries while development occurs in developing countries
Growth deals with quantitative increase in output while development involves qualitative improvement in living standards
Growth is measured in years while development is measured in months
questions.e: Economic growth is simply a rise in the quantity of goods and services (GDP), while economic development includes improvements in people's welfare, structure of the economy and living standards, which is a qualitative change.
questions.p: Growth na just when the amount of goods and services wey country dey produce increase, but development mean say the way people dey live and the structure of the economy dey better too. Na quality change be development, no be just quantity.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT commonly used as an indicator of a country's level of economic development?
o: Military expenditure as a percentage of national budget
questions.e: Life expectancy, literacy rate and per capita income are standard indicators of development used in measures like the Human Development Index. Military spending does not directly measure the welfare or living standards of citizens, so it is not a recognised development indicator.
questions.p: Life expectancy, literacy rate and per capita income na the common things wey dem dey use measure development, like for Human Development Index. Military spending no dey show how people dey live well, so e no be development indicator.

questions.q: Economic planning can best be defined as
o: the buying and selling of goods and services in a free market without government interference
the process by which government controls all means of production in an economy
the process of estimating the annual budget of a country
a deliberate and conscious effort by government to direct and coordinate economic activities to achieve set goals over a period
questions.e: Economic planning involves government deliberately setting goals and coordinating resources and activities over a specific period to achieve national objectives. It is not the same as full state control of production, pure market activity, or just preparing a budget.
questions.p: Economic planning na when government dey purposely arrange and coordinate the economy to reach some goals within time. E no be say government must control everything, or just market wey no get interference, or just budget preparation.

questions.q: Nigeria's First National Development Plan was implemented between which years?
questions.e: Nigeria's First National Development Plan covered the period 1962 to 1968, shortly after independence, aimed at laying a foundation for rapid economic growth and infrastructural development.
questions.p: Nigeria First National Development Plan na from 1962 to 1968, soon after independence, wey dem use try build infrastructure and push economic growth.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common problem militating against successful economic planning in developing countries like Nigeria?
o: Excessive availability of capital for project execution
Inadequate and unreliable statistical data for planning purposes
Abundance of skilled manpower for plan implementation
Too much political stability affecting plan continuity
questions.e: Good planning needs accurate data on population, resources and the economy. In many developing countries, including Nigeria, statistics are often outdated, incomplete or unreliable, making realistic planning and target-setting difficult.
questions.p: To plan well, dem need correct data about population, resources and economy. For many developing countries like Nigeria, the data dem dey old or no complete, so e dey hard to plan well or set realistic target.

questions.q: A country's national income rose from ₦120 billion to ₦150 billion within one year, while its population remained constant at 25 million. What was the percentage increase in per capita income?
questions.p: Per capita income before na 120 billion divide by 25 million = ₦4,800. After, na 150 billion divide by 25 million = ₦6,000. The increase be (6000-4800)/4800 x 100 = 25%.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of subsistence agriculture as practised by many small-scale farmers in West Africa?
o: Use of simple tools like hoe and cutlass
questions.e: Subsistence farming is done on small plots using simple tools mainly to feed the farmer's family, not for export. Large-scale mechanised production for export is a feature of commercial agriculture, not subsistence farming.
questions.p: Subsistence farming na small farm wey dem dey use cutlass and hoe take farm, e dey for family chop, no be for export. Na commercial farming dey do big mechanised farming for export.

questions.q: The type of industry that processes agricultural raw materials such as cocoa, cotton or palm fruits into finished or semi-finished goods is called a(n):
questions.e: Agro-based (agro-allied) industries use farm produce like cocoa, cotton and palm fruits as raw materials to manufacture products such as chocolate, textiles and vegetable oil. Extractive industries deal with minerals, not crops.
questions.p: Agro-based industry na the one wey dey use farm produce like cocoa, cotton and palm fruit take make products like chocolate and oil. Extractive industry na mineral matter, no be crops.

questions.q: Under which land tenure system is land owned by the whole community, while individual members are only given the right to use portions of it for farming?
questions.e: Under communal land tenure, land belongs to the whole community or family group, and members are allotted portions to farm but cannot sell it outright. This is common in many traditional West African societies.
questions.p: Communal land tenure na where the whole community or family dey own the land, dem go just give person portion make e farm am, but e no fit sell am. Na so e be for plenty traditional area for West Africa.

questions.q: 'Land fragmentation', a major problem of agriculture in West Africa, refers to:
o: Irrigation of dry farmland during the dry season
Use of modern machinery on large consolidated farms
Division of farmland into small scattered plots through inheritance
Government acquisition of farmland for industrial estates
questions.e: Land fragmentation happens when farmland is repeatedly shared among children or relatives through inheritance, leaving each person with small, scattered plots. This makes mechanised, large-scale farming difficult.
questions.p: Land fragmentation na when dem dey share farmland give pikin or family members through inheritance, so each person go get small scatter land. Dis one dey make mechanised big farming hard to do.

questions.q: A cocoa farmer in Ondo State harvested 3,600 kg of cocoa beans in a farming season. He sold all the beans at ₦1,350 per kg and spent a total of ₦1,200,000 on farm inputs, labour and transportation for the season. What was his net profit for the season?
questions.p: Total money wey e sell am = 3,600 kg x ₦1,350 = ₦4,860,000. Profit be say minus the ₦1,200,000 wey e spend, e remain ₦3,660,000.

questions.q: Many agro-based industries in West Africa are sited close to large urban centres rather than near the rural farms that supply their raw materials. Which of the following best explains this pattern?
o: Raw materials are actually more available in urban centres than in rural areas
The government forbids industries from being sited in rural areas
Rural areas lack enough farmland to grow raw materials
Urban centres offer better infrastructure, larger markets and skilled labour, which outweigh the cost of transporting raw materials from rural farms
questions.e: Although raw materials come from rural farms, industrialists prefer urban areas because of good roads, electricity, water supply, bigger markets and available skilled workers. These advantages often outweigh the extra cost of moving raw materials to the cities.
questions.p: Even though farm produce dey come from village, industry people like sabi for city because of better road, light, water, big market and skilled workers. Dis advantage pass the extra cost wey dem go use carry the raw material come city.

questions.q: A cottage industry, common in many West African towns, is best described as one that:
o: Is mainly operated by family members at home using simple tools and small capital
Requires heavy imported machinery and large foreign investment
Is owned by government and managed by civil servants
Focuses mainly on exporting finished goods directly to Europe
questions.e: Cottage industries are small home-based businesses, such as local soap-making or weaving, run mostly by family labour with simple tools and little capital. They are not government-owned, do not rely on heavy foreign machinery, and usually serve local markets rather than export.
questions.p: Cottage industry na small business wey dem dey run for house, like soap making or weaving, wey family members dey use simple tools and small money do am. E no be government property, e no need big foreign machine, and e dey mostly serve local market, no be export.

questions.q: In what year was the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) established?
questions.e: ECOWAS was formed in 1975 through the Treaty of Lagos, signed by West African countries to promote economic co-operation and integration in the sub-region.
questions.p: Na for 1975 dem form ECOWAS, through di Treaty of Lagos, make West African kontri dem fit work together for economy matter.

questions.q: OPEC is an acronym that stands for which of the following?
questions.e: OPEC means the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, a body formed by major oil-producing nations to coordinate and unify petroleum policies.
questions.p: OPEC na Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, na di kontri wey dey produce crude oil come form am to arrange dia oil policy together.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is located in which city?
questions.e: ECOWAS has its secretariat headquarters in Abuja, Nigeria, after it moved from Lagos when Nigeria changed its capital city.
questions.p: ECOWAS headquarters dey Abuja, Nigeria, dem move am from Lagos come Abuja after Nigeria change im capital.

questions.q: A member country of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is experiencing a severe shortage of foreign exchange needed to pay for essential imports. Which type of assistance would the IMF most likely provide to this country?
o: A permanent subsidy on all its exports
A grant to fund free education for its citizens
A short-term loan to correct the balance of payments problem
A long-term loan to build new industries
questions.e: The IMF's main role is to give short-term financial support to countries facing balance of payments difficulties, unlike the World Bank, which gives long-term development loans.
questions.p: IMF dey give short-term loan to kontri wey dey find am hard to balance dia foreign payment, e no be im work to build industry or give free school money, na World Bank dey do long-term loan.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the main function of the World Bank?
o: It sets production quotas for crude oil among member states
It provides long-term loans for development projects such as roads, dams and schools
It settles political disputes between African countries
It issues a common currency for its member countries
questions.e: The World Bank mainly gives long-term loans to developing countries to fund infrastructure and development projects like roads, power plants and schools.
questions.p: World Bank dey give long-term loan make kontri fit build road, dam, school and odas, e no be oil quota matter or political wahala be dia work.

questions.q: The African Union (AU) has its headquarters in which city?
questions.e: The African Union, which replaced the Organisation of African Unity, has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
questions.p: African Union headquarters dey Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, na dis organisation replace di old OAU.

questions.q: In the International Monetary Fund (IMF), a member country's voting power is determined mainly by the size of its financial quota contribution. If Nigeria contributes a larger quota to the IMF than another member country, what is the most likely outcome?
o: Nigeria will have greater voting power than that country
Both countries will automatically have equal voting rights
The other country will have greater voting power than Nigeria
Voting power has nothing to do with quota size
questions.e: In the IMF, voting power is linked directly to a country's quota contribution; the bigger the quota a country pays, the greater its voting strength in IMF decisions. Since Nigeria's quota is larger, it will enjoy greater voting power than the other country.
questions.p: For IMF, di money (quota) wey kontri put dey decide how much vote dem go get; bigger quota mean bigger vote. So if Nigeria quota pass di oda kontri own, Nigeria go get more vote pass dem.
